text:
Shipbuilders build you white ships,

falconers raise falcons for you,

bees bring you a honeycomb from the sun,

fishermen fish gold from the sand,

peasants harvest fruits in the fields,

hunters gather deer antlers,

monks copy the gospels for you,

painters present their icons and frescoes,

blacksmiths forge the monastery doors,

juniper trees pour incense into the thuribles,

thujas forge golden censers for you,

but I beg you

only for the acorn

that lies beneath the forest branches,

for a child hungry for joy

when he finds it in winter.

translation.title: Shipbuilders Build You White Ships...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the contrast between royal offerings and the humble winter acorn for a hungry child.
